findings.title: Environment reaches forces by constructor injection, not through `engine.tick()`
findings.description:
- `100-arch:64` says the engine "receives the current agent state array, environmental context, and an optional active-agent subset." `500-arch:52` and `:81` say the server passes the environment query interface to `engine.tick()`. Slice plan `300-slices:27` says "Pass environment context to SimulationManager and engine.tick()."
- The design's per-tick flow (`:100-107`) and `step()` (`:180-187`) call `tick(state, profiles, spatial, dt, forces)` with no environment argument. Instead, `:200-216` gives forces the environment at construction and says this "requires no changes to the BulkForce protocol." The design never acknowledges that it departs from the contract all three parents specify.
- The departure also hides a tick input. `300-arch:35` and `:39` require pure tick functions with explicit inputs so that logging and replay work (`:92`). An environment captured in a closure is an input replay cannot see.
- Required before implementation: either pass the environment (or its query) to `tick()` as the engine architecture specifies, which is a 100-band signature change and must state how forces receive it, or have the PM amend the architecture to adopt constructor injection. If the first option is chosen, the `environment` property and the `TerrainResistance` illustration go too (see the proportionality finding).

findings.title: The `step()` body contradicts the design's own zero-entity rule
findings.description:
- The second `step()` body returns early on `count == 0` before `post_tick()`. But `:291` and `:408` say `post_tick()` must run with zero entities so trail decay continues.
- The design has two conflicting `step()` bodies. `:176-190` is correct (it guards only `tick()`). `:272-288` is not. Implemented as written, trails would stop decaying whenever no agents exist.
- Keep one definition (the `:176-190` form) and delete the other.

findings.title: Post-tick writes are not wired, and the plan's assigned scope is silently narrowed
findings.description:
- Slice plan `300-slices:27` assigns "Handle post-tick environment writes (e.g., stigmergic trail deposits)" to this slice. The design calls `post_tick()` with no arguments (`:105`, `:190`) and names no source for `trail_deposits` or `threat_mutations`.
- `500-arch:104` says the engine returns threat mutations alongside updated agent state. `500-arch:56` defines `post_tick(trail_deposits, threat_mutations)`. The design never says what `tick()` returns or how those values reach `post_tick`.
- The Excluded list (`:42-48`) does not mention this item. Either specify the plumbing (empty pass-through values are acceptable) or add it to Excluded with a reason and have the PM update the plan.

findings.title: Grid resolution and layer selection config are deferred against the plan and the architecture
findings.description:
- Plan `300-slices:27` assigns "seed, grid resolution, layer selection" to this slice's YAML config. The design keeps seed and defers the other two (`:48`, `:153`).
- `500-arch:137` says "the server expects to configure environment via YAML (seed, grid resolution, layer selection)." `500-arch:39` and `:133` make grid resolution configurable per layer per instance. The design's reason, that resolution "belongs to the layers themselves," contradicts those lines.
- Either add the keys now (validated, with unknown layer names failing explicitly), or have the PM change the plan and `500-arch`. Do not drop them silently.

findings.title: The environment seed silently defaults to 42, against the explicit-configuration principle
findings.description:
- `300-arch:47` lists environment seed among "explicit configuration, not hard-coded defaults." This design makes the whole `environment` section optional and substitutes `seed=42` (`:151`, `:250`, and verification step 2 at `:373`).
- The 303 design took the opposite stance for profiles: a missing key is a validation error, not a hard-coded default (`303 design`, Special Considerations). Project rules also prohibit silent fallback values.
- Require the seed at startup, and raise a config error if it is missing. Update verification step 2.

findings.title: World origin is hard-coded to (0, 0), against the architecture's configurable origin
findings.description:
- `500-arch:39` says bounds come from "origin and bounds from configuration," and `500-arch:131` says origin is "configurable … set per instance at startup via configuration." The `build_world_bounds()` helper hard-codes `origin_x=0.0, origin_y=0.0` (`:160-166`).
- The justification at `:169` and `:409` is that the server config has no origin. That is circular: the config lacks the field because this design did not add it.
- Add `origin_x` and `origin_y` to `WorldBoundsConfig` with the same explicit-config treatment as the seed, or have the PM amend `500-arch`.

findings.title: Seasonal parameter has duplicate state and a hard-coded 0.0 labeled "mid-season"
findings.description:
- `_seasonal_parameter` (`:119`) is listed as state but is never read. `step()` takes the value per call with a default of `0.0` (`:176`, `:272`). That is two sources of truth, one of them dead.
- On the 0–1 seasonal cycle (`300-slices:35`), 0.0 is the cycle origin, not "mid-season" as `:198` says. A silent default at a call site is the pattern project rules prohibit.
- Make the parameter required on `step()`, delete the attribute, and have the server pass one named placeholder constant that slice 308 replaces. Correct the description.

findings.title: `environment` is treated as optional, and the design's own rationale contradicts that
findings.description:
- `:220` says the environment is always present to avoid `if environment is not None:` checks, and keeps `Environment | None` "for backward compatibility." But `step()` has two such checks (`:177`, `:189`). The design's own `:407` says every `step()` call must change, so `:410`'s claim that existing tests "continue to work without modification" is false for `step()` callers. The optional type buys nothing.
- Make `environment` a required constructor argument. Test constructors can pass `layers={}`.

findings.title: Speculative API and illustrative future code exceed what this slice needs
findings.description:
- The `TerrainResistance` block is marked "not built here." The `SimulationManager.environment` property (`:216`, `:268-270`) exists so `server.py` can pass the environment to forces, but this slice passes `forces=[]` (`:310`).
- The Value section (`:27`) claims "environment-aware forces enabled," which this slice does not do. `:46` excludes them.
- Cut the illustration and the property. If the FAIL fix passes the environment through `tick()`, the property has no reason to exist. Keep the section to a couple of sentences.

findings.title: The tick-budget NFR is not restated, and environment cost is not measured
findings.description:
- The slice adds `pre_tick` and `post_tick` to every tick. `300-arch:78` sets target rates of 20–60 Hz and overrun behavior against the tick budget. `300-arch:90` requires metrics "to diagnose the bottleneck."
- The success criteria (`:341-357`) restate neither the budget (1/tick_rate, i.e. 50 ms at 20 Hz or about 16.7 ms at 60 Hz) nor any measurement of environment time. The 303 design measured engine tick time separately; this design does not extend that.
- Restate the budget, and measure environment duration separately (DEBUG log or metric, consistent with 303).

findings.title: The 303 and 304 designs disagree on who owns environment-driven forces
findings.description:
- 303 Excluded says "Environment-driven forces — slice 304." 304 Excluded (`:46`) says "Environment-aware behavioral forces — behavior engine initiative (100)." The plan (`300-slices:27`) does not assign forces to 304, so 304's exclusion is correct and 303's pointer is stale.
- Correct the 303 note in a docs commit so the handoff is consistent.

findings.title: The parent plan still says `environment.update()`; the design correctly uses `pre_tick`/`post_tick`
findings.description: - `500-arch:72` and `:137` flagged the `update()` reference for alignment. This design adopts the two-phase interface (`:100-107`), which matches `500-arch:54-58`. The plan entry at line 27 still says `environment.update()`. Update it when this design is accepted.

findings.title: Lifecycle ordering matches the tick cycle
findings.description: - Per tick, `pre_tick` precedes `engine.tick()` and `post_tick` follows it. This matches `300-arch:59-66` and `500-arch:54-58`, and keeps the environment immutable during evaluation.

findings.title: Dependency direction and the environment interfaces match their contracts
findings.description:
- The server depends on the environment package, not the reverse. `build_world_bounds()` converts server config into environment types, which fits `300-arch`'s orchestrator principle.
- The `Environment(bounds, layers)` constructor and `WorldBounds` fields match the 500 slice design's signatures.
